pattern: a knurl's teeth derived from DIN 82, which Python's intent does not state
evidence: The maintainer's decision Q4/Q15 (docs/questions.md): AP242's turned_knurl needs at least three of number of teeth, tooth depth, root fillet, helix angle and hand beside the diameters and pitch (WR2; a diamond's helix angle, WR9), so the Rust rules derive them from the knurling standard and state each in the intent with its source, visible and editable ('standard': 'DIN 82', 'derived': key to source). Values: teeth round(pi x 10 / 1) = 31, the pitch kept at the tool's 1 mm; tooth depth P/2 = 0.5, the depth of DIN 82's 90 degree profile (IS 3403:1981 3.1; assumed, no table gives it); root fillet 0.1, the knurling wheel's crest radius up to 1 mm pitch (IS 6776:1980 4.3); a diamond's helix angle 30 degrees and no hand (DIN 82 type RGE). Checked in tests/threads.rs. Python's knurl states pattern, pitch and diameter only.

pattern: a turned diameter offers ISO 261's coarse and fine threads at its size, Python only its coarse table's
evidence: Stream S3 (specify-core-rust issue #3, the maintainer's): a turned diameter's question asks whether it is a fit, a thread or knurled, so it offers every ISO 261 general-purpose metric thread at that size (M1.6 to M64; standards::ISO_261): the coarse one first, as Python's 'thread:M10' where Python's coarse table has it (and the coarse threads that table stops short of, M14, M30, M60), then the fine pitches as 'thread:M10x1.25', before the knurls. Python offers only the coarse thread of its 13-size table (M1.6 to M24), so the knurl options and choices move along and the new threads are extra; every other option, the default and the prompt are unchanged. The pitches are ISO 261:1998 Table 1's (all three choice columns; the bracketed M30x3/M33x3 and the spark-plug M14x1.25 left out); each choice's callout states pitch and class (M10x1.25-6g) and choosing it writes the same AP242 thread as typing it (tests/thread_choices.rs).
